name: Castellón
title: Castellón Ship UTM | Thickness Gauging for Tankers & Tile Cargo
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at PortCastelló for refinery tankers, chemical carriers, bulkers and container ships: hull, tank and piping UTM surveys.
h1: Thickness Measurement at PortCastelló: Tankers, Bulkers and Ceramic Cargo Ships
intro: PortCastelló serves the refinery and petrochemical plants of the Plana and the ceramic tile industry of the province, so tankers, clay and raw-material bulkers and container ships share a harbour of moderate size. Cargo operations here are steady rather than hurried, which gives room for planned gauging. Ultrasonic thickness technicians travel from India to the ship, with port and terminal passes arranged by the agent, and the scope follows the ship type and terminal rules.

highlights.p: Tankers calling at the liquid bulk berths work under terminal permit rules. We plan ballast tank, deck and piping readings within those rules, so the superintendent receives measured wastage rather than an estimate from the last survey.

Bulkers bringing clay, feldspar and other ceramic inputs discharge into a quay close to the plants. Once a hold is clear, frames, hopper plating and coamings can be read before the next cargo is loaded.
Feeder and short-sea container ships carry the tiles out. Engine-room tanks, sea-water lines and scrubber piping are the most useful spaces to read during a short container call.

port.h: PortCastelló: an industrial harbour on the Valencian coast
p: The Autoridad Portuaria de Castellón runs a harbour a few kilometres from the city, built out into open water behind long breakwaters. The coast around it is low and flat, with the orange groves and ceramic factories of the Plana inland, and the port has been shaped by those industries. Approach and manoeuvring are generally straightforward for the size of ships that call, and pilots board outside the entrance, though a strong easterly swell can limit operations and cause delays in cargo handling or berth allocation.

The traffic is a clear reflection of the local economy. A refinery sits close to the port and handles crude and products, with tankers loading and discharging at the liquid bulk berths, and chemical and biofuel carriers use the same facilities. Ceramics are the second pillar: clay, feldspar, frits and glazes arrive in bulk, and finished tiles leave in containers or general cargo to markets across the world. There is also a gas terminal near the port area and a flow of agricultural cargoes and fertiliser. Cruise traffic is occasional, and the working harbour feels industrial and purposeful more than touristic.

Operations follow cargo programmes rather than timetables, with some ships stopping for a day to discharge and others waiting for a berth at the anchorage for longer. The tide range is small, so draught depends on the dredged depth rather than the water level, and the main seasonal factor is weather. Autumn and winter storms can disrupt anchorage work and sometimes delay arrivals, while summer is calmer and better for launch operations. The size of the harbour keeps the berths close together, which makes it easy for a small team to move between a tanker and a bulk carrier during the same visit.

Tankers and chemical carriers can be gauged alongside at the liquid bulk berths, subject to the terminal's safety rules, the ship's own enclosed-space entry system and the cargo programme. Ballast tanks, voids, cofferdams, deck piping and the shell above the waterline are the usual scope while cargo moves. Bulkers and general cargo ships at the dry cargo quays allow more open working, with holds, coamings and decks reachable once discharging has finished and the hold has been cleaned.

The harbour has no drydock for ships of ocean-going size. Tugs, pilot boats and fishing craft are handled by local workshops, while merchant ships needing steel renewal go to larger yards at Valencia, Cartagena or Barcelona. For these ships, the useful job at Castellón is to establish the wastage picture before the docking, so steel orders and yard bookings reflect measured plating rather than guesses. Anchorage jobs are feasible for short sampling work when a launch and a quiet sea are available, and weather windows are a common planning constraint.
list: Liquid bulk berths — ballast tank, deck, cofferdam and piping readings on refinery tankers and chemical carriers under terminal permit rules
Dry cargo quays for ceramic raw materials — hold frame, hopper and hatch coaming gauging on bulk carriers once holds are clear
Container and general cargo berths — engine-room tank, sea-water line and scrubber piping gauging during tile export calls
Gas terminal berth — hull, ballast tank and deck readings on gas carriers within terminal rules, excluding cargo containment
Castellón anchorage — short sampling jobs on ships waiting for berth or orders, weather and launch permitting
Docking yards at Valencia, Cartagena and Barcelona — gauging started here continues alongside the docking survey

context.h: Port state control and industrial trades at Castellón
p: Port state control at Castellón sits under the Paris MoU and is carried out by the Capitanía Marítima, part of the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante. Tankers and chemical carriers are given additional attention because of their cargoes, and structural condition and corrosion of ballast tanks and deck piping are routine topics of questions. On ships under the Enhanced Survey Programme, a current thickness record shows how steel has changed since the last survey and supports decisions on renewal.

Business in the port is tied to two industries: refining and ceramics. Tanker owners serving the refinery work with charterers who look at vessel condition, and ceramic exporters rely on container and bulk lines that keep their schedules. EU rules affect both: ships calling at EU ports carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime shape decisions on energy and fuel. Older product tankers and small bulk carriers often trade on the same short routes for years, and wear in ballast tanks and hatch covers accumulates quietly until a survey brings it to light.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at PortCastelló
jobs.p: Jobs at Castellón follow the cargo. Tankers bring work shaped by permits and discharge programmes, bulkers bring hold work between cargoes, and container ships bring short engine-room and piping checks. Scope, access and report layout are agreed with the superintendent in advance, so berth hours go on readings. Examples of work that suits this port:
list: Ballast tank and deck gauging on a product tanker discharging at the refinery berth, ahead of a renewal survey.
Hold frame, hopper plating and hatch coaming readings on a bulk carrier after discharging clay or feldspar.
Scrubber overboard pipe and sea-water line gauging on a container ship during a tile loading call.
Pre-docking steel estimate for a chemical tanker, with readings taken here before the yard is selected.
On-hire or pre-purchase condition gauging on a short-sea tanker or bulk carrier.

logistics: The closest international airports are Valencia and Barcelona, each a road journey from Castellón, and Valencia is generally the more convenient for technicians arriving from India through a European or Gulf hub. Castellón's own airport has limited scheduled service. The ship's agent arranges port and terminal passes and a launch for anchorage work. Schengen visas are needed, so please share the vessel's dates early; we confirm mobilisation once visas are issued, as tanker calls can move with cargo programmes.
vessels: Bulk carriers carrying ceramic raw materials

faqs.q: Can a tanker be gauged while discharging at PortCastelló?
faqs.a: Yes, subject to terminal rules. Ballast tanks, voids, cofferdams, deck lines and the shell above the waterline can be read while cargo moves, provided the ship's entry procedure and gas-free conditions are in place. Cargo tank work needs more planning and is best handled when the ship is out of service.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Castellón?
faqs.a: No dock for merchant ships of ocean-going size. Harbour craft and fishing boats use local workshops, while tankers and bulkers needing steel renewal normally go to Valencia, Cartagena or Barcelona. Readings taken at Castellón give you a measured basis for steel estimates and for comparing yard quotations.

faqs.q: Can bulker holds be gauged after clay or feldspar discharge?
faqs.a: Once the hold is empty and cleaned, frames, hopper plating, bulkheads and coamings can be read, if the loading plan leaves the hold free long enough. Dust and residue can make access difficult, so the chief officer's preparation matters. We agree the order of holds with the agent and stop when cargo operations restart.

faqs.q: What can be done at the Castellón anchorage?
faqs.a: Short sampling work is possible when a launch can be arranged and the swell is low. A ship waiting for a berth may move at short notice, so a narrow scope works better than a full survey. Where a long wait is expected, a berth stop gives more time and fewer constraints.

faqs.q: Can gas carriers be gauged at the terminal berth?
faqs.a: We read hull structure, ballast tanks, decks and piping within the terminal's permit rules and the ship's own system, and we do not inspect cargo containment. Because the stay is set by the discharge programme, the scope is agreed in advance with the ship manager and the terminal.
